what: Atits (1,847 in 1901) mainly Tanda and Bikapur; closely resemble the Sannyasi Faqirs, but several cultivate rent-free patches granted by proprietors
quote: The Atits numbered 1,847 persons ... They seem closely to resemble the Sannyasi, Faqirs, but several of them cultivate some patches of land, held rent-free

what: Of 2,051 estates in 1905, 47 owned by Faqirs, Goshains and Bairagis together (combined); revenue-free area of 18,777 acres held mostly by Musalmans, then Brahmans, Bairagis and Goshains
quote: 47 by Faqirs, Goshains and Bairagis, 15 by Kalwars

what: Revenue-free area 18,777 acres, greater part of the non-Muslim remainder held by Brahmans, Bairagis and Goshains
quote: the greater part of the remainder by Brahmans, Bairagis and Goshains

what: Vaishnavism predominant yet only 7.7% Vaishnavites and 5.5% Ramanandis; numerous Faqirs of Ajodhya include many Bairagis, within Vaishnavites, in regularly constituted bodies divided among seven akharas
quote: Among the numerous Faqirs whose home is at Ajodhya there are many Bairagis, who are included in the Vaishnavites ... divided among seven different akharas or orders.

what: Bairagi initiation stages: chhora (3 yrs), bandagidar (3), hurdanga (3), naga (3 yrs wandering to all tirathas on mendicancy), then atith for life; order of precedence: Digambaris, Nirbanis, Nirmohis, Khakis, Niralambhis, Santokhis, Mahanirbanis
quote: the disciple enters on a fourth period of three years called naga ... he reaches the fifth and final stage called atith, which continues till his life's end.

what: Digambaris (naked ascetics) founded by Balram Das 200+ years ago; present head the 11th mahant; small (max 15 resident); revenue-free holdings in Gorakhpur and villages Puraina (Fyzabad) and Kalupur (Tanda)
quote: The Digambaris or naked ascetics are said to have been founded by one Balram Das

what: Largest community; four thoks (Hardwari, Basantia, Ujainia, Sagaria) each with a mahant, over all a single presiding mahant; revenue-free lands in Fyzabad, Gonda, Basti, Partabgarh, Shahjahanpur; moneylending and elephant dealing
quote: The largest community is that of the Nirbanis, who live in the celebrated Hanuman Garhi temple.

what: Nirbanis carry on extensive business as moneylenders and elephant dealers; bought villages with the proceeds; large pilgrim offerings
quote: they carry on an extensive business as money-lenders and dealers in elephants

what: Nirmohi claim descent from Gobind Das of Jaipur; held Janamasthan temple in Ramkot until destroyed; moved to Ramghat; later split with a branch at Guptarghat; Ramghat mahant ninth in succession; lands in Basti, Mankapur, Khurdabad
quote: The Nirmohi sect claim spiritual descent from one Gobind Das of Jaipur.

what: Ash-besmeared Khaki akhara established under Shuja-ud-daula by Daya Ram from Chitrakot; present head 11th from founder; land in Basti and lease of one village in Gonda
quote: The Khaki or ash-besmeared akhara was established in the days of Shuja-ud-daula by one Daya Ram from Chitrakot

what: Niralambhi founded by Birmal Das of Kotah, small, lives on pilgrim offerings
quote: The sect called Niralambhi, or provisionless, dates from the same period, having been founded by Birmal Das of Kotah

what: Santokhis, a small poor sect without endowment, founded under Safdar Jang by Rati Ram of Jaipur; mahant died in 1900 and akhara deserted
quote: The Santokhis or patient faqirs are a small and poor sect without any endowment.

what: Mahanirbanis or dumb faqirs, founded by Parsotam Das from Kotah Bundi under Shuja-ud-daula; seventh mahant; 25 brethren
quote: Lastly come the Mahanirbanis or dumb faqirs ... The present mahant is the seventh in succession

what: Bara Asthan is the headquarters of a fraternity called the Bara Akhara; has lands in this and other districts
quote: the Bara Asthan, the headquarters of a fraternity called the Bara Akhara

what: Temple of Mahant Bhagwan Das-Achari owns revenue-free villages in Basti; Jankighat temple owns several villages; Bara Asthan lands
quote: the temple of Mahant Bhagwan Das-Achari, which owns some revenue-free villages in Basti

what: Mahants of the Hanuman Garhi offered asylum to Europeans and kept troops steady in 1857
quote: A similar offer was made by the Mahants of the Hanuman Garhi, who from the first exerted themselves to keep the troops steady.

what: Ramnaumi in Chait (~400,000), Jhula in Sawan (~300,000), Kartik parikrama and full-moon bathing (~200,000); Hanuman Garhi etc. (ascetic participation not stated)
quote: Of the former the largest is the Ramnaumi in Chait, when some 400,000 persons congregate in the sacred city.

what: Great bathing fair in Chait and Kartik at tank excavated c.1805 by a faqir Nihal Das who brought water from sacred spots
quote: a great bathing fair is held in Chait and Kartik in the tank excavated about 1805 by a faqir, named Nihal Das

what: Fair at the samadh of Gobind Das, a renowned mendicant of a century ago (Aghan)
quote: at the samad of Gobind Das, a renowned mendicant of a century ago, at Ahrauli in Birhar during the month of Aghan

what: Jhula (swinging) fair in Sawan, ~15,000 persons; town name Goshainganj not explained as Gosain foundation here (bazar built by Inchha, Brahman)
quote: The Jhula or swinging fair is celebrated here in the month of Sawan

what: Fair at Deogaon in Pus in honour of Sundar Shah, a Musalman, and Niddhi Chand, a Nanakshahi faqir
quote: in honour of Sundar Shah, a Musalman, and Niddhi Chand, a Nanakshahi faqir.

what: Muafi mahals for the maintenance of Faqirs: 2 in Amsin, 1 each in Surhurpur and Pachhimrath, 2 in Haveli and 3 in Pachhimrath for support of Faqirs
quote: four, comprising two in Amsin and one each in Surhurpur and Pachhimrath, are for the maintenance of Faqirs.

what: Small properties held by Bairagis (Haveli?), pargana Surhurpur etc.; 'Bairagis, Kayasths and Kalwars hold minute properties' in one pargana; chiefly Musalmans, Kayasths and Bairagis own rest in another
quote: the rest is chiefly owned by Musalmans, Kayasths and Bairagis.

what: Tradition: place once held by a Jogi, Subha Nath, killed by Saiyid Salar
quote: it was once held by a Jogi, named Subha Nath, who attracted the attention of Saiyid Salar

what: Jain temples of the Digambari sect (Jain, not ascetic Hindu orders)
quote: These temples are all in the charge of a Gaur Brahman and belong to the Digambari sect.
